subject: Contingent uptime margin & remedy activation flow
messages:
From: Nadia Hassan <nadia.hassan@terraflex.io>
To: Ethan Park <ethan_park@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: procurements@terraflex.io, ops@terraflex.io, laura_bennett@redwoodinference.com
Date: 2026-11-21T08:15:00-07:00
Subject: Request: temporary uptime margin & remedy definitions for go-live

Hi Ethan / Laura,

Thanks again for the call this morning. As we prepare for Terraflex's regional migration (US west -> multi-az) we need a narrowly scoped exception to the standard uptime anchor in the Redwood SLA for the first 90 days after our go-live. Rough outline of what we're asking for: 

- Temporary uptime anchor: 99.8% (instead of 99.95%) for the first 90 days post-cutover.
- Precise remedy trigger: we need a clear, deterministic definition for when credits would activate — ideally based on service-level health across our regional pool rather than ad hoc incident determinations.
- Monthly credit ceiling: please confirm a hard cap (we'd prefer something expressed as a percent of monthly invoice).
- Maintenance/upgrade carveouts: we need scheduled maintenance windows to be clearly excluded and a description of how planned rollbacks are handled.

We want this to be temporary — Terraflex will return to the standard SLA once our traffic normalizes or earlier if the baseline holds. Please share a proposed activation flow (detection -> corroboration -> debtor calculation -> payout) and a draft SLA amendment so procurement can review with legal.

Attaching the migration timeline for context. Looking for a proposal by end of day tomorrow if possible.

Best,
Nadia Hassan
Head of Cloud Ops, Terraflex

From: Ethan Park <ethan_park@redwoodinference.com>
To: Nadia Hassan <nadia.hassan@terraflex.io>
Cc: laura_bennett@redwoodinference.com, monica_patel@redwoodinference.com, ben_carter@redwoodinference.com
Date: 2026-11-21T10:02:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Request: temporary uptime margin & remedy definitions for go-live

Hi Nadia — thanks for the clear note and the timeline. Putting a concise proposal on the table below so procurement/legal have something to react to quickly. We're attaching a draft amendment and an ops runbook excerpt for the activation flow.

High-level proposal (90-day contingent uptime margin):
- Temporary anchor: 99.8% uptime measured at monthly aggregation over recognized Terraflex production routes (region: us-west + us-east where traffic is directed).
- Remedy activation flow (long-form):
  1) Detection: automated monitoring flags sustained unavailability defined as service-error-rate >= 5% at p95 across all routes for >= 15 continuous minutes OR system-level availability below 99.8% for a rolling 6-hour window.
  2) Corroboration: Redwood and Terraflex ops telemetry are correlated (log time ranges + request samplings). If telemetry alignment confirms, an incident ticket is opened and held for a 72-hour RCA window to rule out customer-side configuration issues.
  3) Credit calculation: pro-rated monthly credit equal to (measured cumulative downtime minutes beyond the threshold / total minutes in month) * monthly invoice amount.
  4) Caps: credits per month will not exceed 10% of that month's Redwood invoice for Terraflex. Aggregate credits over the 90-day contingent period capped at 20% of a single monthly invoice.
  5) Payment window: credits applied as invoice offsets in the next billing cycle once finalized.

Maintenance carveouts: pre-scheduled maintenance (>=72 hours notice) is excluded. Emergency maintenance required for security hotfixes will be treated as a carve-in only if we notify within 2 hours and provide post-change diagnostics.

Reinstatement clause: the temporary anchor reverts to the standard 99.95% at day 91 automatically unless both parties agree in writing to extend. Also proposed an automatic early reinstatement if the account sustains >= 95% of committed baseline throughput for any rolling 30-day period.

Attachments: Redwood_SLA_Draft_v1.pdf (SLA amendment draft), ops-runbook.xlsx (remedy activation steps & telemetry checklists).

Next steps: please flag any non-starters (credit cap, detection windows, RCA hold), and if ok we'll produce a redline-ready PDF for legal.

Cheers,
Ethan Park
Senior Sales Engineer, Redwood Inference
--- attachments: Redwood_SLA_Draft_v1.pdf (pdf), ops-runbook.xlsx (xlsx)---

From: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwoodinference.com>
To: Ethan Park <ethan_park@redwoodinference.com>, Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwoodinference.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwoodinference.com>
Date: 2026-11-21T13:45:00-07:00
Subject: INTERNAL: suggested edits to Terraflex proposal (contingent margin)

Team — quick internal notes before we send anything redline-ready to Nadia/procurement: 

1) Detection window: shorten the 6-hour rolling window to 3 hours for availability-based triggers — it makes the activation path tighter for customers and reduces ambiguity during migration spikes.
2) RCA hold: reduce from 72h to 48h for the initial contingent period; keep the 72h if there are cross-region configuration issues.
3) Cap math: I prefer limiting per-month credits to the smaller of (10% invoice) OR (pro-rata of committed monthly spend * 0.15) — helps bound exposure if Terraflex scales very rapidly during ramp.
4) Latency carveout: add an explicit clause for batched inference / warm-up patterns that occasionally push p95 latency above baseline for short windows during cache warming — propose a latency carveout threshold: > 250ms p95 for > 30 minutes triggers a review but not automatic credit unless accompanied by error-rate impact.
5) Auto rollback: clarify the 30-day reversion to standard SLA only if consumption is >= 60% of committed baseline (we should reference the commitment in the contract).

If you all agree, I'll update the draft and prepare a DocuSign powerform for signature on the mutual action plan (MAP). Ben — please run the exposure numbers for the two cap options and share a quick table. Monica — please coordinate with the ops-runbook team to ensure the telemetry fields we require are in the export.

Thanks — Laura
VP, Revenue Operations

Subject: Re: Request: temporary uptime margin & remedy definitions for go-live

Ethan / Laura / team — thanks for the fast turnaround and the detailed proposal. Terraflex is prepared to accept the contingent 99.8% anchor for the first 90 days provided we get two clarifications: 

1) Maintenance carveouts: we need an explicit maximum of two planned maintenance windows per month that may be excluded from availability calculations, and a commitment that Redwood will schedule them outside our primary global deploy windows if possible.
2) Aggregate cap: we accept the 10% monthly cap as a hard limit; the additional aggregate cap (20% of one month's invoice over 90 days) is acceptable as long as the calculation method is spelled out in the amendment.

Once you send an updated redline reflecting Laura's latency carveout language and the maintenance limit above, we'll sign the MAP and route to legal. Attaching the signed (scanned) mutual action plan for speed.

Appreciate the clarity — we'll coordinate ops contacts for telemetry access after signature.

Best,
Nadia
Head of Cloud Ops, Terraflex
